Socio-economic benefits in this project will be achieved in subcomponent 2.4 for Promotion of Sociobiodiversity Value Chains This subcomponent will focus on the development of biodiversity-based economies in support of local communities by fostering sustainable development and enhancing local livelihoods. The project will promote structural actions to support sustainable use practices developed by local communities in critical PAs for conservation, involving approximately 1,500 people. With a focus on promoting gender equity, the project aims to ensure that half of this target audience consists of women, either as direct or indirect beneficiaries. The project will support capacity-building for colective enterprises that empower local residents with new skills and knowledge. Training in sustainable practices and business management enables community members to diversify their income sources and improve their economic stability. This empowerment can lead to greater community resilience, as individuals and families become less reliant on potentially harmful practices like illegal logging or poaching. In turn, this reduces environmental degradation and supports the long-term health of the protected area, contributing to a more balanced and sustainable relationship between people and nature.

to reduce habitat loss and fragmentation, which are the main threats to Brazilian biodiversity, by enhancing the management of critical terrestrial and marine territories for large-scale conservation.
